title: Design: Claude trading desk: a desk-manager session over specialist lanes (market watch, entry review, in-trade management = LTR, exit/post-trade grading), decisions as package-level intents through per-account risk, sandbox/paper first, every decision a point-in-time record the models train on
note: [2026-10-25 16:14Z session_01UKBXozpiJicMHHyMp47MnN] Operator 16:12Z asked whether to scope a 'trading desk manager': lanes for entries, market monitoring, adjustments and exits, managed by one desk session, in a sandbox, with all decisions recorded so the system and models can execute on them. Manager view: yes, scope it as a design after the LTR prototype has run on real trades for a few days, so the design starts from measured review rows (cost/decision, latency, hit rate). Dispatch after LTR-4 is live. [2026-10-25 ~16:20-16:22Z session_01UKBXozpiJicMHHyMp47MnN] OPERATOR INPUTS (chat, close paraphrase): (1) the desk RELIES ON THE REPO for context: the repo produces specific outputs (a per-decision 'decision packet') so Claude is applied only to the important judgment and context, not to building context or redoing research each time; this keeps a consistent pattern and makes outputs fit the datasets the models train on and the live trade management uses. (2) Balance usage vs learning: do not waste usage on routine decisions, but do use powerful models where we learn: 'at least some of them should be Opus, or maybe it's enough if Opus is doing the review and not the actual live management'. (3) Make sure the lanes have what they need to perform live management. (4) Timeframe: see how small we can get; '15 minutes is feasible in any case', and drive it lower. MANAGER PROPOSAL to carry into the design: L0 deterministic packet + due-watch (no model); L1 Haiku gate; L2 Sonnet live decisions on the packet; L3 Opus on escalations PLUS a sampled share of decisions re-judged blind by Opus as teacher labels for distillation, and the weekly grading. Measure end-to-end latency (bar close -> decision recorded) in the LTR prototype as the baseline for the 15m target. [2026-10-25 ~16:27Z session_01UKBXozpiJicMHHyMp47MnN] OPERATOR (chat, close paraphrase): (5) scope a lane that STAYS LIVE for short-timeframe trades (10 min to 1 h holds): what would it cost, could it be profitable, which timeframes are feasible, and can we build a flow that works. (6) Decision packets are the SAME data feed for Claude and the ML models: Claude infers a decision from the packet, the ML models learn from Claude's inference (Claude decisions = training data), and when ML does live trade management, Claude's recommendations are included in that pipeline (as an input). DESIGN MUST ANSWER for (5): measured cost/decision and latency from the LTR prototype; standing-lane cost per hour at 1m/5m/15m cadence incl. context growth and rotation; edge net of full cost at those horizons from existing scalp harnesses (ict_scalp, chop_scalp, fvg_range) or new Stage-0 units; break-even = usage cost per trade vs expected R x risk. For (6): one packet schema shared by Claude and ML; Claude label vs realized outcome both kept (Claude is a teacher, never ground truth); Claude-as-feature only where Claude is available at inference time (CJ design Q2 'Allow as a feature later'); point-in-time info_cutoff on every row. [2026-10-25 17:36Z session_01UKBXozpiJicMHHyMp47MnN] Operator ~17:35Z: push the desk design faster; prioritize it above other builds (not replace, may supersede some). Dispatched NOW (Opus $14) instead of after LTR-4 data; design uses first-run measurements (LTR-3 run, packet build ~36 s) and marks the rest unmeasured. Reshapes: CJ-2 now waits on it (dataset schema = desk packet schema); LTR-6/8/9 re-scoped by its intent->per-account-risk path; LTR-5 grading folds into its grading section. [2026-10-25 18:36Z session_01UKBXozpiJicMHHyMp47MnN] Design v0 merged #20140 (390040b9). Observation: operator approves the desk design (answers or defers remaining Q3 VM-side model call, Q4 live entry skip); due_by 2026-11-01. Operator answers already DECIDED: feeds = repo + logged exception; sandbox = shadow bybit_1. Build rows DESK-0..13 (§10) to be filed after operator review. [2026-10-26 ~06:45Z OPERATOR popups, verbatim, relayed by manager session_01HAysMLfF9dYpi92YMqYxEq] (1) design: "Approve as the build plan (Recommended)" -- rows DESK-0..DESK-14 are the build plan, built in critical-path order; later stages still pass their own gates. (2) design Q2 (entry skips): "I so one but also like the idea isn't just to reject entries that are coming from the strategies. The ideas to generate entries by reviewing in monitoring the life markets that's moral aiming than just a veto over that the strategy is going to" -- read as: entry-review skips stay shadow until the DESK-7 replay passes, AND the desk's goal is to GENERATE entries from live-market monitoring, not only veto strategy entries. This contradicts design § 2.3 ('Never in any enum: ... a new entry') -> new row DESK-15-ENTRY-GENERATION amends the design. (3) design Q1 (VM-side model call for sub-15 min): "Not now (Recommended)". Context: operator 06:40Z 'this is only the first step of the trading desk project ... keep pushing that forward, but ... everything there is also logged correctly'. [2026-10-26 06:52Z manager CORRECTION] OPERATOR 2026-10-26 ~06:50Z, verbatim: "just to be clear about the entry stage of the desk project, like, the goal isn't for Claude to be reviewing the entries. That's, I mean, we can have that also, that's nice, but when I say the trading desk does entries, I mean that they find trades that the system isn't finding. So, like, I don't even know what that restriction on should Claude be able to deny an entry, like, where that even came from. That's just, like, not the design at all. Completely wrong direction." The manager's reading of the 06:45Z answer ('entry skips stay shadow') is WITHDRAWN. Where the restriction came from: design v0 (#20140, 2026-10-25, lane-authored) defined the entry role as entry review over strategy packages (take/skip/delay) with market watch limited to delay/veto_candidate, and § 2.3 'Never in any enum: ... a new entry'; § 11 Q2 then asked whether skip should apply. That framing is wrong. Corrected direction: the desk's entry stage GENERATES new trades the strategies are not finding (row DESK-15, now rank 2 on the desk path); entry review of strategy packages is optional, secondary, record-only; the MD-DESK-SKIP proposal is dropped from DESK-13. [2026-10-26 06:56Z manager] OPERATOR VISION 2026-10-26 ~06:55Z, verbatim: "the whole idea here with the trading desk is that we're trying to build a system where Claude isn't just weighing in on the system's trades. Claude is, the Claude trading desk is driving the trading, and the MLs, the systems MLs that we're building are learning from that Claude decision-making how to do it themselves so that we can eventually remove Claude from the flow and have only our own AIs doing the trading. But the whole point is to have Claude pushing the whole trading operation so that we can use that as the basis for teaching the MLs." Consequence: design v0 frames the desk as advisory/shadow over the strategies' trades; that framing is superseded. v1 must make the desk the DRIVER of the trading operation (finds and enters trades, manages and exits them), still through each account's RiskManager, the promotion ladder (offline evidence -> paper soak -> real money under operator-granted mandates) and the per-trade refusal path, with every desk decision recorded as a teacher label for the ML students (distillation design, CJ rows) so the system's own models can eventually replace Claude. Rewrite owned by DESK-15 (widened).
